controls.label: Color + brightness
controls.qualification: The star's color, darker where mirc saw its surface dimmer in the infrared · 2 to 24 September 2011, mapped in this project
controls.notes: λ Andromedae in its own color, darker where interferometry of 2 to 24 September 2011 shows its surface darker. The interferometer resolved the star's disc, so the places of the dark regions, in longitude and latitude, are measured, down to about 21° of the surface. The map is of infrared light, where the darkest region gives 35% less light than the brightest; it is drawn as a much darker tone of the star's own hue, and the Surface map's scale has the measured values. How dark the spots are in visible light, and their color, are not measured. The star is drawn as it faced the Earth on 14 September 2011, at the tilt and pole direction Martinez et al. (2021), ApJ 916, 60 measured. The 34° of longitude that faced the Earth on none of the nights are drawn at the mean. Spots come and go within weeks or months: this is the star then. The darkening toward the edge is the Color dataset's limb law, drawn 1.5 times as strong. A reduction made in this project with the authors' code and calibrated nights, not their published map.

controls.label: Surface map
controls.qualification: Mapped in this project · mirc, september 2011
controls.notes: Where λ Andromedae's surface was darker and brighter in infrared light on 6 nights, 2 to 24 September 2011, worked out in this project from what the mirc interferometer measured. The star turned by 146° between the first night and the last, so one surface is fitted to all of them, with the size, tilt, pole direction and period Martinez et al. (2021), ApJ 916, 60 measured. Both the longitudes and the latitudes of the dark regions are fixed by the data, down to about 21° of the surface; nothing finer is. The 34° of longitude that faced the Earth on none of the nights hold the mean, inside the black line. The colors are a scale of brightness in one infrared band, not the star's color or temperature. A reduction made in this project with the authors' code and calibrated nights, not their published map.
controls.legendNote: Darker: dimmer than the mean of the surface seen; white: brighter. Black line: the edge of what never faced the Earth on these nights.

controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Color from its measured spectrum. The disc itself is unresolved; darkening toward the edge from a published law.
controls.notes: The color of the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 1125). The spin axis's direction on the sky is a display convention. The darkening toward the edge is the power law I(mu) = mu^0.231 that Martinez et al. (2021), ApJ 916, 60 fit to the star's resolved disc (CHARA/MIRC H band, 1.5-1.7 um; not a visible band).
